newsitem.title: GERMANY: German debt rallies, poised to move still higher.
newsitem.headline: German debt rallies, poised to move still higher.

text.p: A U.S. bond rally infected the German market, sending prices higher in afternoon trading and setting the stage for still more gains next week, dealers said.
The March Bund futures contract closed with gains of 40 basis points at 102.52, after having traded between 102.06 and 102.61 during the session.
The benchmark cash bond, maturing 2007, was up at 102.71 compared with Thursday's 102.36 close.
While dealers said the market may first face a consolidation early next week, the stage appears to be set for further gains after that.
After a lacklustre morning spent waiting for U.S. jobless numbers, the U.S. Treasury market's positive reaction to the data breathed new life into the German market.

"Fundamentally the mood has certainly improved in the German bond market with the catastrophic German jobless numbers raising hopes the Bundesbank may ease interest rates again," said one trader, adding that the U.S. jobs data also helped.
U.S. jobs data showed little inflationary pressures, which pushed out the spectre of another interest rate increase.
With few German economic data scheduled for release next week, the market will again be focusing on U.S. data for new trading impules.
